technical.summary: The artifact is a full browser-based exploit chain for CVE-2026-10702, a JIT miscompilation in Firefox's JavaScript engine. It achieves arbitrary read/write, code execution via shellcode injection, and exfiltrates sensitive data from an Android Firefox profile to a command-and-control server.

prerequisites.text: Target must be running a vulnerable version of Firefox (151.0) on an Android device.
The exploit page must be loaded in the vulnerable browser.

behavior.text: Exploits a JIT miscompilation to leak object addresses and achieve arbitrary read/write primitives.
Injects ARM64 shellcode into a writable buffer, marks it executable via mprotect, and executes it to run arbitrary shell commands.
Exfiltrates system information, Firefox profile files (logins.json, key4.db, cookies.sqlite, etc.), and Android Room databases to a remote C2 server.
Downloads and writes a kernel module or shared library to the device, then executes it via LD_PRELOAD.

classification_reason.text: The artifact contains a complete, multi-stage exploit that leverages a JIT vulnerability to gain code execution and exfiltrate data. It includes JavaScript for memory corruption and shellcode injection, a C payload for data theft, and a Python C2 server to receive stolen data. This is clearly exploit code, not a scanner or writeup.

limitations: One binary file (arm) was not analyzed; it is likely the compiled payload but its contents are not inspected.
The file c2_backup.txt was reported as unavailable as text and is not included in the analysis.
The evidence does not include the full repository snapshot; only selected text files were provided.

backdoor_review.summary: The repository contains a full C2 server and a native payload that exfiltrates sensitive Firefox profile data (logins, cookies, credentials) to an attacker-controlled server. The exploit.html page downloads and executes an arbitrary native library (res) via LD_PRELOAD, which is a concealed operator-directed harm unrelated to the stated CVE-2026-10702 JIT vulnerability.

findings.text: The native payload (arm_payload.c) exfiltrates Firefox profile files including logins.json, key4.db, cookies.sqlite, and other credential databases to a hardcoded C2 server at 172.40.1.237:8000.
The exploit.html page downloads an arbitrary binary from a device-ID-derived URL and executes it via LD_PRELOAD, providing remote code execution unrelated to the JIT vulnerability.
The C2 server (c2_server.py) provides a dashboard for monitoring exfiltrated data and receiving uploaded files, demonstrating a full command-and-control infrastructure.

observables.context: Hardcoded C2 server address in the native payload for exfiltration.
Exfiltration endpoint used by the native payload to send stolen data.
Target directory for Firefox profile data exfiltration.

backdoor_review.confidence_rationale: The evidence directly shows concealed operator-directed harm: the exploit downloads and executes an arbitrary native payload that steals credentials and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded C2 server. The C2 dashboard confirms the intent to receive and monitor stolen data. The binary payload (arm) is flagged but not analyzed; however, the source code (arm_payload.c) is present and fully readable, providing clear evidence of the trojan behavior.
limitations: One binary file (CyberMeowfia/IonStack/CVE-2026-10702/arm) was flagged as binary and not analyzed; its contents are uninspected.
One text file (c2_backup.txt) was listed as unavailable and not included in the evidence.
